notes.text: Use a wider pan so the fillets stay in one layer; the court-bouillon takes 5 minutes longer to reach temperature.

move.title: 170 to 180°F, and hold it
move.body: Poaching cooks fish in liquid kept well below a simmer, so it sets evenly from edge to center and stays moist. You'll build a court-bouillon (a quick aromatic poaching liquid), bring it to 170–180°F, hold it there with the thermometer while the salmon cooks to 145°F, and serve it with a cold dill and yogurt sauce made while the liquid steeps.

why.title: Court-bouillon
why.body: Water simmered for 15 minutes with onion, celery, carrot, lemon, and herbs. Acid and aromatics season the fish from the outside while it poaches.

why.title: Why 170–180°F
why.body: Below 160°F the fish cooks too slowly to be practical; at a simmer the outside overcooks and squeezes out white albumin before the center is done. Holding 170–180°F gives an even, moist set.

why.title: Lower the fish into hot, not boiling
why.body: Fish added to a rolling boil seizes at the surface. Bring the liquid down to 180°F first; it drops a few degrees when the fish goes in, then climbs back.

why.title: Carryover
why.body: A thick fillet keeps cooking a few degrees after it leaves the liquid. Pull it at 140–145°F and let it rest 3 minutes.

wrong.sign: White curds formed all over the fish
wrong.fix: The liquid was too hot. It's safe; next time hold it under 180°F.
The liquid dropped too low. Raise the heat a notch and recheck every 2 minutes.
Lift with a wide slotted spatula under the whole fillet, or poach on a strip of parchment you can lift by the ends.

quiz.q: What temperature does the poaching liquid hold?
Why not poach at a simmer?
choices: The outside overcooks and squeezes out albumin

quiz.q: When do you pull a thick salmon fillet?
choices: When it flakes apart in the pan

steps.text: Slice the onion, celery, and carrot thin and the first lemon into rounds. Put them in the skillet with the water, bay, peppercorns, parsley stems, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered.
Meanwhile, zest and juice the second lemon and mince the garlic. Stir the yogurt, dill, zest, 1 tablespoon of the juice, mustard, garlic, and salt. Chill.
Pat the salmon dry and keep it in the fridge until the liquid is ready.
Wash your hands and the board.
Lower the heat until the court-bouillon reads 180°F.
Lower in the salmon with the slotted spatula, skinned side down, in one layer. Hold the liquid at 170–180°F, adjusting the heat as you check it.
Check the thickest portion in its center.
steps.tip: Pull at 140°F if you're resting it covered; it climbs to 145°F.

steps.text: Lift the fillets onto a paper-towel-lined plate. Rest 3 minutes.

steps.look: Evenly coral all the way through, moist, with no white beads.
